manifest.name: @hanxu131/dshacp
manifest.description: Zed-first ACP v1 server driving DeepSeek Harness (DSH): standalone stdio bridge with token streaming, tool calls, approval, plan, and session management

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run build && npm run test:unit

bundle.text:
# DSHACP bundle patch — the layer `dsh plugin add @hanxu131/dshacp` contributes
# to a profile, applied after `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` and before the profile's
# own cordis.patch.yml. Declared by package.json's `dsh.bundle.patch`.
#
# This is the BUNDLE form of the DSHACP composition. The STANDALONE form (the
# `dshacp` bin) composes the same surface from two other shipped files:
# `cordis.yml` (the root config, which lists the same rows below) plus
# `dshacp.patch.yml` (the overlay that follows the insert). A bundle has no
# root config of its own — the profile already provides `dsh-base` — so this
# one patch both inserts the DSHACP-owned rows and applies the web-app-style
# disable list in a single layer.
#
# Two differences from the standalone form are forced by the install model:
#   * the app row references this package by name (`@hanxu131/dshacp`) instead of
#     the relative `./lib/index.js`, so Node resolves the installed package;
#   * the agent-presets row leaves `roots` empty: the dsh launcher's profile
#     boot injects the shipped preset root itself, exactly as it does for the
#     web/headless profiles.
#
# Everything else mirrors `cordis.yml` + `dshacp.patch.yml`; keep them in sync
# when the standalone form changes.

# ── insert the DSHACP-owned rows ───────────────────────────────────────────

- insert:
    # The preset roster: each ACP session composes its agent from one preset
    # (standard / cordis / code / minimal). `default` is the starting mode.
    # `roots` is intentionally empty — the dsh profile boot fills the shipped
    # `config/agent-presets` root; the plugin appends `~/.dsh/.agent-presets`
    # (user trust) automatically.
    - id: agent-presets
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
      config:
        default: standard
        roots: []

    # The DSHACP profile startup latch (help/--dump-config must not claim stdio).
    - id: dshacp-app-startup
      name: '@hanxu131/dshacp/startup'

    # Standard preset subagent tools with `modelSelectionSettings: true` need
    # this host row (0.1.2).
    - id: subagent-model-selection
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings'
      config:
        enabled: false

    # NOTE: the `ssh` row (@linxin666/dsh-ssh) is deliberately absent from the
    # bundle form. It is itself a DSH bundle whose ssh2 dependency needs a
    # native build script, which would break the one-command `dsh plugin add`
    # (pnpm ≥10 ignores builds until approved). Add SSH to a profile the
    # standard way — `dsh plugin --profile <name> add @linxin666/dsh-ssh` — it
    # joins the layer stack on its own. The standalone bin still mounts SSH
    # out of the box (see cordis.yml).

    # The DSHACP app: the widened ACP bridge over the base composition.
    # Referenced by package name so the installed package resolves; the package
    # `main`/`exports["."]` points at lib/index.js.
    - id: dshacp
      name: '@hanxu131/dshacp'
      config:
        # How long a pushed permission request waits for the client before
        # rejecting (fail-closed).
        approvalTimeoutMs: 600000
        # How long an elicitation (ask_user_question) waits for the user before
        # failing the tool call closed.
        elicitationTimeoutMs: 1800000
        # Opt-in hybrid mode: with DSHACP_HYBRID=1 AND a client that advertises
        # fs.writeTextFile (Zed does), `write` delegates to the client editor.
        hybridFileWrites: !!js "process.env.DSHACP_HYBRID === '1'"

    # The host-side Cordis plugin runner: provides `dynamicCordisRunner` +
    # `cordisInspect` for the `cordis` agent preset. Headless-safe.
    - id: cordis-host-runner
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-host-runner'

    # qwenmm vision understanding (qwen-mm-plugins api). `failOnStartupError:
    # false` keeps the process bootable when uvx / a DashScope key is absent —
    # the MCP tools simply fail in their card.
    - id: mcp-qwen-mm-plugins-api
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: qwen-mm-plugins-api
        transport: stdio
        command: uvx
        args:
          - '--from'
          - 'qwen-mm-plugins[api] @ git+https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-MM-Plugins.git@qwen-mm-plugins-api-v1.0.3'
          - 'qwen-mm-plugins-api'
        cwd: !!js process.cwd()
        failOnStartupError: false

# ── surface-specific values the base deliberately omits ─────────────────────

# DSHACP is headless: stdout is reserved for ACP JSON-RPC, and no HMR exists.
- id: hmr
  disabled: true

# The deployment persona (presets shadow it per agent).
- id: system-prompt
  config:
    persona: >-
      You are a coding assistant powered by the {{model}} model. Your working directory is {{cwd}}. Your bash tool runs under a file sandbox — a `[sandbox: file access denied …]` result is policy, not a command bug.

      Verify your work by running the code or tests. Keep answers brief and factual.

# Sessions persist beside the project (Zed launches from the project root, so
# `./.sessions` is per-project); DSH_SESSIONS_ROOT overrides.
- id: session-persistence-jsonl
  config:
    root: !!js "process.env.DSH_SESSIONS_ROOT ?? './.sessions'"

# ── the agent plane moves behind agent presets ─────────────────────────────
#
# Every row below composes what ONE agent contributes to the host registries.
# The base keeps them for the single-session TUI; DSHACP disables them here and
# lets each session mount a preset instead. Host-plane rows that MUST stay
# host-plane (shell-env, the job/goal/subagent/workflow/tool REGISTRIES,
# token-meter, tool-subagent-report) are deliberately NOT disabled.

- id: tool-bash
  disabled: true

- id: tool-pwsh
  disabled: true

- id: tool-jobs
  disabled: true

- id: tool-fs
  disabled: true

- id: tool-fs-search
  disabled: true

- id: tool-str-replace-editor
  disabled: true

- id: skill-filesystem
  disabled: true

- id: tool-skill
  disabled: true

- id: tool-goal
  disabled: true

- id: plan-mode
  disabled: true

- id: compaction-basic
  disabled: true

- id: command-compact
  disabled: true

- id: tool-result-pruner
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-control
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-list-agents
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-fork
  disabled: true

- id: workflow-worker-thread
  disabled: true

- id: tool-workflow
  disabled: true

- id: tool-ralph
  disabled: true

- id: agent-instructions
  disabled: true

- id: tool-todo
  disabled: true

- id: tool-web
  disabled: true

readme.section: DSHACP — 让 Zed 用上 DeepSeek
readme.text:
> DSHACP 是 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的一个**插件**。装好之后，你就能在
> [Zed](https://zed.dev) 编辑器里直接和 DeepSeek 对话、让它帮你读文件、写代码、跑命令。

[English](README.en.md)

---

readme.section: 这是什么？（先花 30 秒看懂）
readme.text:
一句话：**DSHACP 是 Zed 和 DeepSeek 之间的"翻译官"。**

```
你（在 Zed 里打字提问）
        │
        ▼
   Zed 编辑器（代理面板）

Zed 自带的是 Claude、GPT 等模型的连接方式。给 DSH 装上 DSHACP 插件之后，Zed 会
多出一个叫 **DSH** 的"外部代理"，它背后就是 DeepSeek。

readme.section: 装好之后，你能干什么
readme.text:
- 在 Zed 里直接问 DeepSeek，回答像打字机一样逐字流出来
- 让它读文件、写代码、跑命令，每一步操作都能在界面上看到
- 它要做有风险的操作（比如改文件）时，会先弹窗问你"允许吗"
- 对话自动保存，下次打开还能接着聊

readme.section: 和官方 `dsh --profile acp` 有什么区别？
readme.text:
DSH 0.1.2 起，官方在 npm 上同时提供 **`@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`**（`dsh --profile acp`）和本插件
**`@hanxu131/dshacp`**（`dsh --profile dshacp`）。两者都走 ACP v1 / stdio，但定位不同，**不要装进同一个 profile**。

readme.section: 和官方 `dsh --profile acp` 有什么区别？
readme.text:
| | 官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp` | 本插件 DSHACP |
|---|---|---|
| **启动** | `dsh --profile acp` | `dsh --profile dshacp` |
| **面向谁** | CI、脚本、自动化流水线 | [Zed](https://zed.dev) 等交互式 ACP 客户端 |
| **会话** | 基本 `new` / `prompt` / `cancel` | `list` / `load` / `resume` / `delete` / `close` 等完整生命周期 |
| **流式** | 以回合级文本为主 | **token 级** `assistant/chunk`、reasoning、工具输入输出 |
| **审批** | 较简 | 推送 `request_permission` 到客户端，支持 allow once / always |
| **配置** | 无 | Zed 面板可选 **model / thinking / permission / mode**（agent preset） |
| **扩展** | 无 | slash 命令、plan、`ask_user_question`（elicitation）、HTTP MCP 转发、可选 hybrid 写文件 |
| **安装** | DSH 自带 / 官方 profile | `dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp` |

readme.section: 和官方 `dsh --profile acp` 有什么区别？
readme.text:
一句话：**官方 ACP 够用且克制，适合「机器调机器」；DSHACP 是加宽桥，把 DSH 的交互能力完整暴露给 Zed。**

```
Zed ──ACP──► dsh --profile dshacp ──► @hanxu131/dshacp（本插件）

CI  ──ACP──► dsh --profile acp  ──► @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp（官方，互不混装）
```

---

readme.section: 1. DeepSeek Harness（DSH）已装好
readme.text:
打开终端（Terminal），输入：

```sh
dsh --version
```

readme.section: 2. Zed 编辑器
readme.text:
到 <https://zed.dev> 下载安装。本插件只配合 Zed 使用。

---

readme.section: 第 1 步：安装 DSHACP 插件
readme.text:
打开终端，输入这一条命令：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp
```

> 首次安装会直接装到 npm 上的最新版（`latest`），无需指定版本号。

readme.section: 更新到新版本
readme.text:
已装过的用户升级时，**推荐直接用 `update` 命令**（无需手动写版本号）：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp update @hanxu131/dshacp
```

为了让它稳定生效，先在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里**永久关闭发布年龄门控**，
加一行 `minimumReleaseAge: 0`：

```sh

readme.section: 打开 ~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp/pnpm-workspace.yaml，在 autoInstallPeers 那行下面加上：
readme.text:
minimumReleaseAge: 0
```

> 没有这行时，npm 上刚发布的新版本（官方默认"发布年龄"需满数天）会被 pnpm 的
> 供应链门控挡下，`update` 会误报 `Already up to date`。设为 `0` 即永久关闭门控，
> 之后 `update` 会正常追到最新版。

升级完成后，**退出并重开 Zed 里的 DSH 会话**（或重启 `dsh --profile dshacp` 进程），
新代码才会被加载。

> 备选：若不想改配置，也可显式带版本号
> `dsh plugin --profile dshacp add "@hanxu131/dshacp@^0.2.0"`；但由于 `add` 存在
> lock 锁定、`update` 更省心，日常仍建议用上面的 `update` 方式。

readme.section: 从旧版 `acp` profile 迁移（0.2.0 起）
readme.text:
DSH 0.1.2 起，官方 `dsh --profile acp` 留给 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`（自动化专用 ACP）。
DSHACP 改用独立 profile **`dshacp`**，不要与官方 `acp` profile 混装。

若你曾把本插件装进 `~/.dsh/profiles/acp`：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile acp remove @hanxu131/dshacp
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp
```

然后把 Zed 配置里的 `"args": ["--profile", "acp"]` 改成 `"dshacp"`，并重启 DSH 会话。

readme.section: 第 2 步：在 Zed 里添加 DSH
readme.text:
1. 打开 Zed，按 `Cmd + ,`（macOS）或 `Ctrl + ,` 打开 **Settings（设置）**。
2. 左侧找到 **AI** → **External Agents（外部代理）**。
3. 点击 **Add Custom Agent（添加自定义代理）**，把下面这段粘贴进去：

```jsonc
{
  "agent_servers": {
    "DSH": {
      "type": "custom",

> 这里 `command` 是 `dsh`（不是 `dshacp`）：Zed 会用 `dsh --profile dshacp` 启动
> 我们刚才装好的那个 profile。`env` 留空即可。

**成功的样子**：Zed 的代理列表里出现一个叫 **DSH** 的选项。

readme.section: 第 3 步：开始第一次对话
readme.text:
1. 打开 Zed 的代理面板（Agent Panel，通常在编辑器右侧）。
2. 在代理/模型下拉框里选 **DSH**（不是 Claude、GPT）。
3. 输入一句简单的话，比如：

> 你好，请告诉我你能做什么。

---

readme.section: 1. 提示 `command not found: dsh`
readme.text:
说明 DSH 没装好，回到"开始之前"第 1 条，先 `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`。
如果用的是 nvm 管理 Node，装完 **重开一个新终端窗口** 再试。

readme.section: 2. 一进对话就报缺密钥 / 401 之类的错
readme.text:
密钥是 DSH 侧配置的（由维护者负责），不是这个插件的问题——找维护者在 DSH 里补上
DeepSeek API Key 即可。

readme.section: 3. 点了"允许"，它还是不动
readme.text:
- 确认 Zed 里选的是 **DSH** 代理
- 打开 Zed 命令面板，输入 `dev: open acp logs`，看有没有报错信息

readme.section: 4. 换项目之后，之前的对话不见了
readme.text:
每次对话都保存在**当前项目目录**下的 `.sessions` 文件夹里（换项目 = 新一批对话）。
想统一存到别处，可以设置环境变量 `DSH_SESSIONS_ROOT`（见下文）。

readme.section: 5. 重新 `add` 插件却没升级到新版本
readme.text:
这是 **pnpm 的版本锁定/发布年龄门控**导致的，不是命令写错：

- `dsh plugin add` 底层就是 pnpm 的 `add`。**只要 profile 目录里的 `pnpm-lock.yaml`
  已经锁定了某个版本，即使 npm 上出了更新版，`add` 也不会主动跳版本**——它会返回
  `Already up to date`。
- 新发布的版本在 pnpm 的"最低发布年龄"（minimum release age，默认数天）之内时，
  `update` 也会被供应链安全门控挡下，同样显示 `Already up to date`。

**推荐做法：永久关闭门控 + 用 `update` 追新**（见「第 1 步 → 更新到新版本」）。
在 `~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 加一行 `minimumReleaseAge: 0` 后，
升级命令就固定为：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp update @hanxu131/dshacp
```

readme.section: 5. 重新 `add` 插件却没升级到新版本
readme.text:
若不愿改配置，也可以临时显式带版本号（profile 名 `acp`、包名 `@hanxu131/dshacp`，
从 `0.1.3` 升到 `0.1.4`）：

```sh

readme.section: ✅ 临时可行：显式带上目标版本范围
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile dshacp add "@hanxu131/dshacp@^0.1.4"

readme.section: ❌ 无效：不带版本、或只写 @latest，都会被锁定/门控挡住
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add "@hanxu131/dshacp@latest"
```

升级完记得**重启 Zed 里的 DSH 会话**（或重启 `dsh --profile dshacp` 进程）让新代码生效。

---

readme.section: 进阶：给想深入了解的人
readme.text:
<details>
<summary>展开查看（环境变量、模型选择、独立二进制、源码构建、协议细节等）</summary>

readme.section: 环境变量
readme.text:
| 变量 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `DSH_SESSIONS_ROOT` | 会话保存目录（默认 `./.sessions`） |
| `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` | `workspace-write`（默认，会弹确认框）或 `danger-full-access`（不再弹确认框） |
| `DSHACP_HYBRID` | 设成 `1` 开启混合模式：写文件时交给 Zed 展示 diff 供你审查 |

readme.section: 在 Zed 里选模型 / 思考强度 / 权限 / 模式
readme.text:
装好之后，Zed 的 DSH 面板里可以直接选 **model**、**thinking strength**、**Permissions**、**mode**。
也可以在配置里写死默认值（下面是示例，模型名以面板里实际显示的为准）：

```jsonc
"DSH": {
  "type": "custom",
  "command": "dsh",
      "args": ["--profile", "dshacp"],

`model` 的写法是 `提供商:模型`；只写模型名也可以，程序会自动找到对应的提供商。

**Permissions**（`permission`）控制 sandbox 与审批策略，可选值通常为：

- `workspace-write`（默认）：沙箱限制工作区外写入，敏感操作会弹出确认框
- `danger-full-access`：无沙箱限制，也不再弹出确认框

**mode** 是 agent preset（工具集 / 技能配置），与 **Permissions** 无关；不要与 ACP 文档示例里「mode 控制 permission」的语义混淆。

readme.section: 独立二进制安装（另一种方式，不用 DSH profile）
readme.text:
如果你不想用 DSH profile，也可以直接装成独立的 `dshacp` 命令：

```sh
npm install -g @hanxu131/dshacp
```

然后在 Zed 里把 `command` 改成 `dshacp`、`args` 留空。功能与插件方式一致。

readme.section: 从源码构建（给开发者）
readme.text:
```sh
git clone git@github.com:ECHOUniverse/dshacp.git
cd dshacp
npm install
npm run build   # 编译 TypeScript

readme.section: 本地联调到 DSH dshacp profile（给开发者）
readme.text:
**不要用 `npm link` 链源码目录**——会把 repo 的 `node_modules/` 带进 profile，导致 Cordis 插件双份加载（`deployment:persona already registered`）或缺少依赖（`schemastery not found`）。

在仓库根目录执行：

```sh
./scripts/dev-link-dsh-profile.sh   # build → npm pack → 装进 ~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp
```

改代码后重新跑该脚本，并**重启 Zed 里的 DSH 会话**。恢复 npm 发布版：

```sh
./scripts/dev-unlink-dsh-profile.sh
```

readme.section: 可选功能
readme.text:
- **粘贴截图让 DeepSeek 看**：装好 `uv`/`uvx` 和 qwenmm 插件后，可以直接把截图粘进
  Zed 让模型"看图"。详见 `docs/P5-image-paste-qwenmm.md`。
- **远程 SSH**：`dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @linxin666/dsh-ssh`。
- **混合模式**：`DSHACP_HYBRID=1`，文件改动以 diff 形式呈现，逐块审查。

readme.section: ACP 能力面（协议层，给开发者）
readme.text:
- 客户端 → 服务端：`initialize`、`session/new`、`session/load`、`session/resume`、
  `session/list`、`session/delete`、`session/close`、`session/set_config_option`、
  `session/prompt`、`session/cancel`
- 服务端 → 客户端：`session/request_permission`、`session/request_elicitation`、
  `session/update`
- 刻意不实现：`authenticate`/`logout`、`session/set_mode`、`fs/*`、`terminal/*`

readme.section: 目录结构（给想改代码的人）
readme.text:
- `src/bin.ts` — 独立二进制的启动入口
- `src/index.ts` — 应用主体（ACP 桥接）
- `src/bridge.ts` — ACP v1 桥接（会话、流式、审批等）
- `src/codec.ts` — 编解码
- `cordis.yml` / `cordis.patch.yml` / `dshacp.patch.yml` — 组合配置（`cordis.patch.yml`
  是插件安装时生效的那一层）
- `tests/` — 测试

</details>

---

readme.section: DSHACP — Use DeepSeek inside Zed
readme.text:
> DSHACP is a **plugin** for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Once installed, you can chat
> with DeepSeek directly inside the [Zed](https://zed.dev) editor and have it read
> files, write code, and run commands for you.

[中文](README.md)

---

readme.section: What is this? (30-second version)
readme.text:
In one sentence: **DSHACP is the "translator" between Zed and DeepSeek.**

```
You (typing questions in Zed)
        │
        ▼
   Zed editor (agent panel)

Out of the box, Zed knows how to talk to Claude, GPT, and a few others. Once you
add the DSHACP plugin to DSH, Zed gains a new **external agent** named **DSH**,
backed by DeepSeek.

readme.section: What you get after installing
readme.text:
- Chat with DeepSeek right inside Zed; replies stream in word by word
- Let it read files, write code, and run commands — every action is visible
- Before it does anything risky (like editing a file), it asks "allow?"
- Conversations are saved automatically and can be resumed later

readme.section: How is this different from official `dsh --profile acp`?
readme.text:
Since DSH 0.1.2, npm ships both **`@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`** (`dsh --profile acp`) and this plugin
**`@hanxu131/dshacp`** (`dsh --profile dshacp`). Both speak ACP v1 over stdio, but they target
different jobs — **do not install both bridges into the same profile**.

readme.section: How is this different from official `dsh --profile acp`?
readme.text:
| | Official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp` | DSHACP (this plugin) |
|---|---|---|
| **Launch** | `dsh --profile acp` | `dsh --profile dshacp` |
| **Audience** | CI, scripts, automation pipelines | Interactive ACP clients such as [Zed](https://zed.dev) |
| **Sessions** | Basic `new` / `prompt` / `cancel` | Full lifecycle: `list` / `load` / `resume` / `delete` / `close` |
| **Streaming** | Mostly turn-level text | **Token-level** `assistant/chunk`, reasoning, tool I/O |
| **Approval** | Minimal | Pushes `request_permission` to the client (allow once / always) |
| **Config** | None | Zed panel: **model / thinking / permission / mode** (agent presets) |
| **Extras** | None | Slash commands, plans, `ask_user_question` (elicitation), HTTP MCP forwarding, optional hybrid file writes |
| **Install** | Bundled with official profile | `dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp` |

readme.section: How is this different from official `dsh --profile acp`?
readme.text:
In short: **official ACP is deliberately narrow for machines; DSHACP is a widened bridge for humans in Zed.**

```
Zed ──ACP──► dsh --profile dshacp ──► @hanxu131/dshacp (this plugin)

CI  ──ACP──► dsh --profile acp  ──► @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp (official — keep separate)
```

---

readme.section: 1. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) installed
readme.text:
Open a terminal and run:

```sh
dsh --version
```

If it prints a version number, DSH is ready. If it says `command not found`,
install DSH first:

```sh
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
```

> The DeepSeek API key is configured on the DSH side by the maintainer — you
> don't need to worry about it in this tutorial.

readme.section: 2. The Zed editor
readme.text:
Download and install it from <https://zed.dev>. This plugin only works with Zed.

---

readme.section: Step 1: Install the DSHACP plugin
readme.text:
In a terminal, run this one command:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp
```

> First-time installs fetch the latest version (`latest`) directly — no version
> number needed.

readme.section: Updating to a newer version
readme.text:
If you already installed it and want to upgrade, **prefer the `update` command**
(no version number needed):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp update @hanxu131/dshacp
```

For this to work reliably, **permanently disable the release-age gate** in the
profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` by adding one line:

```sh

readme.section: open ~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp/pnpm-workspace.yaml, add below the autoInstallPeers line:
readme.text:
minimumReleaseAge: 0
```

> Without this line, a version released only recently (pnpm's default
> "minimum release age" is a few days) gets blocked by supply-chain gating and
> `update` wrongly reports `Already up to date`. Setting it to `0` disables the
> gate permanently, so `update` always fetches the latest version.

After upgrading, **quit and reopen the DSH session in Zed** (or restart the
`dsh --profile dshacp` process) so the new code is actually loaded.

readme.section: open ~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp/pnpm-workspace.yaml, add below the autoInstallPeers line:
readme.text:
> Alternative: if you'd rather not edit the config, you can pin the version
> explicitly — `dsh plugin --profile dshacp add "@hanxu131/dshacp@^0.2.0"`. But
> because of pnpm's lock behavior, `update` is the easier day-to-day choice.

readme.section: Migrating from the old `acp` profile (0.2.0+)
readme.text:
Since DSH 0.1.2, official `dsh --profile acp` is reserved for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`
(automation-only ACP). DSHACP uses its own profile **`dshacp`** — do not install both
bridges into the same profile.

If you previously installed into `~/.dsh/profiles/acp`:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile acp remove @hanxu131/dshacp
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp
```

Then change Zed's `"args": ["--profile", "acp"]` to `"dshacp"` and restart the DSH session.

Breaking it down:

readme.section: Migrating from the old `acp` profile (0.2.0+)
readme.text:
- `dsh plugin` = use DSH's plugin manager
- `--profile dshacp` = install into a profile named `dshacp` (created automatically if missing)
- `add @hanxu131/dshacp` = install the DSHACP plugin

**How to know it worked**: the command finishes without `error`, ending with
something like `Done in Xs`.

> To double-check, run `dsh --profile dshacp --dump-config` — you should see
> `dshacp`-related config rows in the output.

readme.section: Migrating from the old `acp` profile (0.2.0+)
readme.text:
**Remote SSH is optional** and not included by default. If you want it, add one
more plugin:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @linxin666/dsh-ssh
```

readme.section: Step 2: Add DSH to Zed
readme.text:
1. Open Zed and press `Cmd + ,` (macOS) or `Ctrl + ,` to open **Settings**.
2. Find **AI** → **External Agents** in the sidebar.
3. Click **Add Custom Agent** and paste the following:

```jsonc
{
  "agent_servers": {
    "DSH": {
      "type": "custom",

> Here `command` is `dsh` (not `dshacp`): Zed launches `dsh --profile dshacp`, which
> boots the profile we just installed. Leave `env` empty.

**How to know it worked**: an option named **DSH** appears in Zed's agent list.

readme.section: Step 3: Start your first conversation
readme.text:
1. Open Zed's agent panel (usually on the right side).
2. In the agent/model dropdown, pick **DSH** (not Claude/GPT).
3. Type something simple, like:

> Hi, tell me what you can do.

**How to know it worked**:

- The reply streams in word by word (not all at once)
- When it wants to perform an action, an "allow / deny" confirmation pops up

If it gets stuck, see "Troubleshooting" below.

---

readme.section: 1. `command not found: dsh`
readme.text:
DSH isn't installed. Go back to "Before you start" item 1 and run
`npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`. If you use a version manager like nvm, **open a
new terminal window** and try again.

readme.section: 2. It errors out with a missing key / 401 as soon as a conversation starts
readme.text:
The key is configured on the DSH side (the maintainer's responsibility), not by
this plugin — ask the maintainer to add the DeepSeek API key to DSH.

readme.section: 3. You click "allow", but nothing happens
readme.text:
- Make sure you selected the **DSH** agent in Zed
- Open Zed's command palette and run `dev: open acp logs` to look for errors

readme.section: 4. Your conversations disappear after switching projects
readme.text:
Conversations are saved under a `.sessions` folder in the **current project
directory** (a new project = a new set of conversations). To store them all in
one place, set the `DSH_SESSIONS_ROOT` environment variable (see below).

readme.section: 5. Re-running `add` doesn't upgrade to the new version
readme.text:
This is **pnpm's version-locking / release-age gating**, not a mistake in the command:

- `dsh plugin add` wraps pnpm's `add`. Once the profile's `pnpm-lock.yaml` has
  pinned a version, `add` **won't jump to a newer version** even if one exists on
  npm — it just prints `Already up to date`.
- Versions younger than pnpm's "minimum release age" (a few days by default) are
  also blocked by supply-chain gating, so `update` shows `Already up to date`
  too.

readme.section: 5. Re-running `add` doesn't upgrade to the new version
readme.text:
**Recommended fix: disable the gate permanently and use `update`** (see
"Step 1 → Updating to a newer version"). Add `minimumReleaseAge: 0` to
`~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp/pnpm-workspace.yaml`, then the upgrade command is simply:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dshacp update @hanxu131/dshacp
```

If you'd rather not edit the config, pin the version explicitly instead (profile
`acp`, package `@hanxu131/dshacp`, upgrading `0.1.3` → `0.1.4`):

```sh

readme.section: ✅ Works ad hoc: pin the target range explicitly
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile dshacp add "@hanxu131/dshacp@^0.1.4"

readme.section: ❌ Does NOT work: no version, or only @latest — both are blocked by locking/gating
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @hanxu131/dshacp
dsh plugin --profile dshacp add "@hanxu131/dshacp@latest"
```

After upgrading, **restart the DSH session in Zed** (or restart the
`dsh --profile dshacp` process) so the new code takes effect.

readme.section: Advanced: for those who want to dig deeper
readme.text:
<details>
<summary>Expand (environment variables, model selection, standalone binary, building from source, protocol details, …)</summary>

readme.section: Environment variables
readme.text:
| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `DSH_SESSIONS_ROOT` | Where sessions are stored (default `./.sessions`) |
| `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` | `workspace-write` (default, shows confirmations) or `danger-full-access` (no confirmations) |
| `DSHACP_HYBRID` | Set to `1` to enable hybrid mode: file writes are delegated to Zed as reviewable diffs |

readme.section: Choosing model / thinking strength / permissions / mode in Zed
readme.text:
Once installed, you can pick **model**, **thinking strength**, **Permissions**, and
**mode** directly in Zed's DSH panel. You can also pin defaults in the config (the
example below is illustrative — use whatever the panel actually shows):

```jsonc
"DSH": {
  "type": "custom",
  "command": "dsh",
      "args": ["--profile", "dshacp"],

The `model` value is `provider:model`; a bare model id also works and resolves
to the provider that owns it.

readme.section: Choosing model / thinking strength / permissions / mode in Zed
readme.text:
**Permissions** (`permission`) controls the sandbox and approval policy. Typical values:

- `workspace-write` (default): sandbox restricts writes outside the workspace; sensitive operations prompt for confirmation
- `danger-full-access`: no sandbox restrictions and no confirmation prompts

**mode** is the agent preset (tooling / skill set) and is separate from **Permissions**; do not confuse it with the ACP doc example where a `mode` option controls permission behavior.

readme.section: Install as a standalone binary (alternative, no DSH profile)
readme.text:
If you'd rather not use a DSH profile, you can install the standalone `dshacp`
command instead:

```sh
npm install -g @hanxu131/dshacp
```

Then in Zed set `command` to `dshacp` with an empty `args`. The functionality is
identical to the plugin method.

readme.section: Build from source (for developers)
readme.text:
```sh
git clone git@github.com:ECHOUniverse/dshacp.git
cd dshacp
npm install
npm run build   # compile TypeScript

readme.section: Link a local build into the DSH dshacp profile (for developers)
readme.text:
**Do not `npm link` the source tree** — it pulls the repo's `node_modules/` into the
profile, which duplicates Cordis plugins (`deployment:persona already registered`)
or breaks imports (`schemastery not found`).

From the repo root:

```sh
./scripts/dev-link-dsh-profile.sh   # build → npm pack → install into ~/.dsh/profiles/dshacp
```

After code changes, re-run that script and **restart your Zed DSH session**. To restore
the registry release:

```sh
./scripts/dev-unlink-dsh-profile.sh
```

readme.section: Optional features
readme.text:
- **Paste a screenshot for DeepSeek to read**: after installing `uv`/`uvx` and the
  qwenmm plugin, you can paste screenshots into Zed for the model to "see". See
  `docs/P5-image-paste-qwenmm.md`.
- **Remote SSH**: `dsh plugin --profile dshacp add @linxin666/dsh-ssh`.
- **Hybrid mode**: `DSHACP_HYBRID=1` — file edits appear as reviewable diffs.

readme.section: ACP surface (protocol layer, for developers)
readme.text:
- Client → server: `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/load`, `session/resume`,
  `session/list`, `session/delete`, `session/close`, `session/set_config_option`,
  `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`
- Server → client: `session/request_permission`, `session/request_elicitation`,
  `session/update`
- Intentionally not implemented: `authenticate`/`logout`, `session/set_mode`,
  `fs/*`, `terminal/*`

readme.section: Layout (for contributors)
readme.text:
- `src/bin.ts` — entry point for the standalone binary
- `src/index.ts` — app plugin (the ACP bridge)
- `src/bridge.ts` — ACP v1 bridge (sessions, streaming, approval, …)
- `src/codec.ts` — codecs
- `cordis.yml` / `cordis.patch.yml` / `dshacp.patch.yml` — composition config
  (`cordis.patch.yml` is the layer applied by the plugin install)
- `tests/` — tests

</details>
